entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Priarius was a king of the Lentienses, a sub-tribe of the Alemanni, in the 4th century. He is mentioned by Ammianus Marcellinus. In 378 CE, Priarius fought the Western Roman Empire at Battle of Argentovaria, near Neuf-Brisach, France, in which he was defeated and killed.

Priarius's reign was marked by the ongoing pressure of the Goths, who had been raiding Roman territories since the 3rd century. His struggle against the Roman Empire was part of a larger pattern of migration and conflict in the Late Antique period.

The Battle of Argentovaria was a significant turning point in the decline of the Western Roman Empire, marking the beginning of the end of Roman control in Gaul. Priarius's defeat led to the establishment of the Alamannic Kingdom, which would go on to play a major role in European politics for centuries to come.

Priarius's legacy is also tied to the complex relationships between the various Germanic tribes of the time, including the Alemanni, Goths, and Visigoths. His actions and decisions had far-reaching consequences for the balance of power in the region, shaping the course of European history for generations to come.

The fact that Priarius's name has survived to the present day is a testament to the enduring legacy of the Late Antique period, a time of great upheaval and transformation that continues to fascinate historians and scholars today.
